mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60d returns in more than 60% of quarters when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and signals economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their 12-month moving averages signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both below 12-month moving average simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both proxies are below their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 4% signals aggressive monetary tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% AND CPIAUCSL > 4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between RSAFS and GDPC1, where rising personal savings (RSAFS) coincides with rising GDP (GDPC1), supports future consumption and corporate investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of absolute levels.
failure_condition: The correlation between RSAFS and GDPC1 turns negative or S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive when this correlation is positive.
